**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 28

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Full parallels to this rule are attested across the Prātimokṣa and Vibhaṅga texts of all surviving Vinaya recensions. Within the Pali canon, it corresponds to rule 28 in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha and the Bhikkhu Parivāra. In other traditions, it appears as Sarvāstivāda Pācittiya 25 (extant in Chinese and Sanskrit), Mūlasarvāstivāda Pācittiya 27 (in Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit manuscripts), Mahīśāsaka Pācittiya 29, Dharmaguptaka Pācittiya 28, and Mahāsāṅghika/Lokottaravāda Pācittiya 27. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus reflects extensive Pali-internal phrasing shared especially with its companion rule Pācittiya 27 (over 6,000 matching characters across segments §0.1–2.13), as well as the Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka (Kd 15) and several other Vibhaṅga rules [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language matches identified by DharmaNexus align the text with the Tibetan translation of the Mūlasarvāstivāda *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-3) and related treatises such as the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2) and the *Vinayasūtra* (D4117) [DharmaNexus]. Modern English translations include that by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
